# Psalm 58 — Disagreement Log
**Generated by:** SOPHIA | **Threshold:** <70% word overlap

---

## 58:1 (overlap: 0%)

- **EMET:** For-the-choirmaster. Al-Tashcheth. Of-David. A-Miktam.
- **LOGOS:** For the choirmaster. According to Do Not Destroy. A Miktam of David.
- **PNEUMA:** For the music director. A psalm of David, to the tune of 'Do Not Destroy.'

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

---

## 58:4 (overlap: 0%)

- **EMET:** The-wicked are-estranged from-the-womb; the-ones-speaking lies go-astray from-birth.
- **LOGOS:** The wicked are estranged from the womb; they go astray from birth, speaking lies.
- **PNEUMA:** These wicked people are born sinners; even from birth they have lied and gone their own way.

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

---

## 58:8 (overlap: 0%)

- **EMET:** Let-them-flow-away like-waters [that] go; let-him-bend his-arrows [till] they-are-as-if cut-off.
- **LOGOS:** Let them vanish like water that runs away; when he aims his arrows, let them be blunted.
- **PNEUMA:** May they disappear like water into thirsty ground. Make their weapons useless in their hands.

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

---

## 58:10 (overlap: 0%)

- **EMET:** Before your-pots can-feel the-thorns — whether green or-blazing — He-sweeps-them-away.
- **LOGOS:** Sooner than your pots can feel the heat of thorns, whether green or ablaze, may He sweep them away!
- **PNEUMA:** God will sweep them away, both young and old, faster than a pot can feel the blazing fire of thorns beneath it.

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

---

## 58:11 (overlap: 0%)

- **EMET:** The-righteous rejoices when-he-sees vengeance; his-feet he-washes in-the-blood of-the-wicked.
- **LOGOS:** The righteous will rejoice when he sees the vengeance; he will bathe his feet in the blood of the wicked.
- **PNEUMA:** The godly will rejoice when they see injustice avenged. They will wash their feet in the blood of the wicked.

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

## 58:9 (overlap: 6%)

- **EMET:** Like-a-snail [that] melts [as] it-goes, like-the-miscarriage of-a-woman [that] does-not see the-sun.
- **LOGOS:** Let them be like the snail that dissolves into slime, like the stillborn child who never sees the sun.
- **PNEUMA:** May they be like snails that dissolve into slime, like a stillborn child that never sees the sun.

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.
